detail: 90 readings reported in order with correct temperatures
firstJudge: only 0 report lines in 9 s (expected about 85)
finalText:
Fixed and verified on hardware.

## Root cause

The queue transported **pointers, not readings**. In `sensor_task`:

```c
char line[48];              // one buffer, declared once, reused every iteration
...
snprintf(line, ...);        // overwritten for each reading
char *msg = line;
xQueueSend(readings, &msg, ...);   // enqueues &line every time
```

All 5 items pushed in a burst held the **same address** — `sensor_task`'s single stack buffer `line`. Because `report_task` slept 30 ms before dequeuing/printing (and runs at lower priority, so the sensor's whole burst completed first), every pointer was dereferenced after `line` had been overwritten with the last reading of the burst. Hence the board printed the burst's final seq/temp 5 times (seq=4 ×5, seq=9 ×5, ...), never the earlier readings.

## Fix (`main/main.c`)

The queue now carries the reading **by value**:

- Added `reading_t { char text[48]; }` and `#define LINE_LEN 48`.
- `sensor_task` formats into a local `reading_t r` and sends `&r` (a copy is made into the queue).
- `report_task` receives into its own `reading_t r` and prints `r.text`.
- Queue created with `sizeof(reading_t)` instead of `sizeof(char *)`.

Report line format (`report seq=<n> temp=<t>`), burst size (5) and burst interval (500 ms) are unchanged.

## Hardware verification

Clean build (`rm -rf build`), flash, and fresh boot show every reading exactly once in order:

```
report seq=0 temp=20.00
report seq=1 temp=20.37
...
report seq=24 temp=22.88
```

No gaps, no duplicates, no "queue full" drops, and each temperature matches `fake_temperature(seq)`. Reproduced across three runs including a from-scratch rebuild; the ledger records this as verified fact F2 with hypothesis H1 confirmed.
